Respondent no. 1 filed Title Suit no.2 of 1989 in the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court, Dhaka, Against Rupali Bank Limited and others for declaring the order of his dismissal from service as illegal and for other consequential reliefs. The trial court decreed the suit on 1.7.1990. Rupali Bank Limited then filed Title Appeal no.239 of 1990 in the Court of the District Judge, which was ultimately heard on transfer by the 5th Court of the Additional District Judge. The appeal was dismissed by the judgment and decree dated 11.8.1993 and against thereof Rupali Bank Limited obtained rule in Civil Revision no.3277 of 1993, but the High Court Division upon hearing discharged the rule. 

 7. In view of the aforesaid decision we are to see the reliefs, which the plaintiff is required to get if the order of his dismissal from service is presumed to be illegal. The relief's needed by him will be a decree declaring the order of the dismissal from service as illegal and that being not sufficient he will need a decree for mandatory injunction directing his employer to reinstate him to the post he was holding at the time of his dismissal from service.  8. Obviously finding difficulty to assail this legal position. Mr. A. K. M. Nazrul Islam, learned advocate for the respondent no. 1, reads the prayer portion of the plaint as amended subsequently and submits that respondent no. 1 in his plaint did not pray for any mandatory injunction, but prayed for a declaratory decree and for a permanent injunction as a consequential relief to the effect that the defendant-Bank be restrained from disturbing the plaintiff in his service. It is the admitted position that the plaintiff is out of his office consequent to the order of his dismissal from his service and therefore the said decree for permanent injunction cannot be an effective relief if the plaintiff gets the declaratory decree to the effect that his dismissal from service is illegal. Under the circumstances the plaintiff ought to have prayed for a decree of mandatory injunction under section 55 of the Specific Relief Act, but, as we have already held, clause (e) of section 56 of the Specific Relief Act is a bar to get the decree for mandatory injunction in the case of the plaintiff. 

 9. In view of the legal position as discussed above we need not decide the issue as to whether the dismissal from service in question was illegal, but we must hold that the suit is not maintainable on the ground that a declaratory decree will not be enough and that a decree for mandatory injunction necessary as a consequential relief is barred under the law. We, therefore, find that neither the trial court nor the appellate court nor the High Court Division considered this vital issue, which cuts at the root resulting the suit not maintainable as framed. The suit ought to have been dismissed on this issue. 

 10. In the result, the appeal is allowed without cost. The judgment dated 8.3.1999 passed by High Court Division in Civil Revision no.3277 of 1993 are set aside and consequently both the judgments and decrees of the courts below are set aside. Title Suit no. 2 of 1993 of the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court no.2, Dhaka, is dismissed without cost.
